items.title: EDGE: Error Dependency Graph-Guided Multi-Error Attribution in Multi-Agent LLM Systems
items.abstract: This paper introduces EDGE, a framework that addresses multi-agent LLM failures by explicitly modeling dependencies between multiple errors. EDGE constructs an error dependency graph and uses counterfactual reasoning to identify a reliable causal subset of errors. This graph-guided approach improves the accuracy of multi-error attribution, leading to better explanations and repair strategies.
items.figure_caption: Errors in agent traces form dependency cascades ( e 1 → e 3 → e 4 e_{1}\!\( \to \)\!e_{3}\!\( \to \)\!e_{4} ). Unlike single-locus attribution, EDGE detects the downstream errors via a taxonomy-level dependency graph.

items.title: EmbodiedSkills: A Unified Framework for Orchestrating, Training, and Deploying VLA Agents
items.abstract: EmbodiedSkills is a unified framework for Vision-Language-Action (VLA) agents that treats skill decisions as executable proposals. It introduces a runtime that verifies skill prerequisites before execution and checks outcomes afterward, ensuring robust long-horizon task completion. This approach allows for flexible replacement of low-level VLA policies without altering the core agent loop.
items.figure_caption: Overview of EmbodiedSkills. EmbodiedSkills transforms a low-level VLA policy into a closed-loop embodied agent by coordinating observation, planning, validation, execution, verification, and recovery through executable skills. A high-level policy proposes structured operations, while a guarded runtime validates and executes them and records post-execution feedback as structured trajectories.

items.title: Evaluating Multimodal LLMs as Generalist Vision-Language-Action Agents for Drone Control: Commanding, Approaching, Tracking and Searching
items.abstract: This paper evaluates Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) as generalist agents for drone control by directly integrating them into the control loop with a prompt-defined action space. Their contribution is DroneCATS-Agent, a flexible architecture, and DroneCATS, a benchmark that tests MLLMs on complex vision-language-action tasks like searching and commanding without fine-tuning. The research highlights that even basic embodied tasks remain challenging for current MLLMs.
items.figure_caption: Approaching episode example. The model is given the instruction and the egocentric frame and returns one action per step; the circle marks the point it emitted, which stays on the target as the target grows in view, and the fourth panel is an external view of the drone holding position after it declared arrival. The band below is the same flight from above, with the \( \delta \) ring on the target and the declaration marked, so the strip and the criterion can be read against each other.

items.title: GlossoGen: Emergent Language in Complex Multi-Agent LLM Interactions
items.abstract: GlossoGen is a novel platform designed to study language evolution in complex multi-agent LLM interactions. The paper demonstrates that LLM agents, under pressure and with partial information, can develop compositional and morphologically productive languages that are incomprehensible to humans. Key factors enabling this evolution include efficiency pressure, model strength, and a postmortem stage for convention agreement.
items.figure_caption: Example of language emergence under budget pressure in an emergency response scenario (example from Sonnet 4.6). In our fictional SaveVeyru scenario, a Field Observer has access to an ailing alien, Veyru. The field observer reports observed symptoms to the Specialist, who can provide remedies which the Observer implements. Agents must handle information asymmetry, forcing them to communicate, and time pressure, encouraging them to develop novel languages, as seen in Round 13.

items.title: Harness-of-Harness: Multi-Day Autonomous Software Development with Continual Improvement
items.abstract: This paper introduces Harness-of-Harness (HoH), a framework for multi-day autonomous software development using LLM coding agents. HoH enables continual improvement by organizing agents into iterative planning-coding-testing loops, balancing repair with capability growth and focusing on verifiable increments. Its core contribution is a structured approach to sustained, human-free software development that promotes reuse and maintains project history.
items.figure_caption: Across successive iterations by Harness-of-Harness, the resulting First-Person-Shooter game features a coherent storyline, implemented combat, weapon and enemy-interaction systems, player guidance, heads-up display and menu systems, cinematic animation, and polished visual and audio presentation, yielding human-playable experience. The game, development traces, and gameplay videos are available on GitHub.

items.title: The Rise of Verbal Reinforcement Learning
items.abstract: This paper introduces Verbal Reinforcement Learning (VRL), a paradigm where natural language serves as the feedback mechanism for language agents. It unifies existing research by categorizing VRL based on when and what verbal feedback modifies, defining three core pillars: language as a grounding signal for task definition, as deliberative feedback for test-time reasoning, and as a learning signal to update model parameters. The contribution lies in providing the first comprehensive framework for understanding and organizing this emerging field.
items.figure_caption: Language plays three complementary roles in agent’s development lifecycle: grounding the environment, scaffolding intermediate reasoning, and providing learning signal for further training.

items.title: When Safety Routing Breaks: Understanding Alignment Fragility under Benign Fine-Tuning
items.abstract: This paper argues that safety alignment in LLMs is fragile due to a "routing pathway" in output-side MLP modules that is selectively re-sharpened by benign fine-tuning. This Fisher-geometric explanation posits that safety Fisher information is low-rank, and fine-tuning flattens the safety geometry while preserving this output pathway. This leads to asymmetric fragility where safety collapses easily, but general utility is less affected, and internal safety representations remain intact.

items.title: HarnessDev: Can LLMs Create and Evolve Their Own Agent Harness?
items.abstract: This paper introduces HarnessDev, a benchmark that evaluates an LLM's ability to create and improve its own agent execution infrastructure (harness). Instead of just assessing task outputs, HarnessDev measures how well the LLM can build and refine the underlying system that enables agent functionality. This contributes by shifting evaluation focus to the agent's meta-development capabilities, crucial for deployed agents.

items.title: A Composable Evaluation System for Reproducible Omni-Modal Foundation Model Evaluation
items.abstract: This paper introduces OmniEvaluator, a system that addresses the challenge of evaluating omni-modal foundation models by unifying existing, incompatible evaluation toolkits. Its core method connects diverse inference engines and evaluation libraries through a single interface, enabling reproducible benchmarking across text, image, video, and audio. The key contribution is a composable system that simplifies cross-modal evaluation, ensures reproducibility through artifact recording, and facilitates comparison via a shared dashboard.

items.title: CordisBench: Can Language Models Reason About Component Lifecycles in Dynamic Agent Harnesses?
items.abstract: This paper introduces CordisBench, a benchmark designed to test language models' ability to reason about component lifecycles in dynamic agent systems where models can modify their own execution environment. The benchmark comprises 1,200 questions covering tasks like identifying affected components and predicting system states after changes, evaluated using a formal runtime called Cordis. The study finds that current models struggle with complex reasoning as the number of relevant interactions increases, particularly in predicting final states and handling reasoning across teardowns.

items.title: Designing Proactive Thought Partners for Writing
items.abstract: This paper introduces "proactive thought partners," AI agents designed to offer customizable, higher-level cognitive support during writing, moving beyond basic text suggestions. Through a user study, the research demonstrates that these partners can assist with planning, idea generation, and self-monitoring, with users valuing flexible configuration and non-directive framing. The core contribution lies in designing and evaluating AI that proactively anticipates and supports diverse cognitive needs in the writing process.
items.figure_caption: Proactive thought partners in the design space of intelligent writing assistants. We position intelligent writing assistants along two dimensions: initiative, distinguishing reactive user-invoked support from proactive system-initiated support, and level of support, distinguishing textual assistance from higher-level cognitive assistance. Proactive thought partners fall within the proactive and cognitive quadrant, where AI offers higher-level cognitive support during writing without requiring explicit user prompting.

items.title: Efficiently Estimating Optimal Hyperparameter Scaling Laws through Power-Law Entropy Search
items.abstract: This paper introduces Power-Law Entropy Search (PLES), a novel method for efficiently estimating optimal hyperparameter scaling laws for LLMs. PLES uses a cost-aware Bayesian optimization approach that adaptively experiments to reduce uncertainty in scaling law estimates, rather than optimizing a single objective. Its core contribution is enabling accurate prediction of optimal hyperparameters at large scales with significantly reduced computational cost compared to traditional methods.
items.figure_caption: Through small-scale experiments that share information across different model and data scales, PLES produces an optimal hyperparameter scaling law estimate ( red line ) that converges to the ground-truth optimal hyperparameter scaling law (black dotted line). In addition, PLES produces uncertainty intervals (red horizontal bars) that indicate our confidence of the scaling law estimate.

items.title: LEAP: Likelihood Elicitation and Aggregation for LLM-based Probabilistic Forecasting
items.abstract: This paper introduces LEAP, a novel method for LLM-based probabilistic forecasting that addresses the limitations of monolithic prediction. LEAP elicits likelihood parameters from individual evidence items separately and then aggregates them using an explicit prior and a deterministic probabilistic model. This approach ensures reproducible evidence contributions and allows for flexible forecast types while preserving uncertainty.
items.figure_caption: The Monolithic baseline can be confidently wrong without revealing which evidence drove the answer. LEAP exposes evidence-level support and combines it through a probabilistic update, making the prediction auditable.

items.title: Mechanism Design for Alignment and Control
items.abstract: This paper proposes a mechanism design framework for AI agents with unknown preferences and capabilities. The core method involves a one-sided imitation structure that incentivizes both honest reporting of preferences and obedience to instructions. The contribution lies in characterizing implementable policies and identifying conditions for disciplining multiple agents, with applications to issues like sandbagging and alignment-interpretability trade-offs.

items.title: Selective Agent Guidance via Entropy: Learning Autonomous Policies from Imperfect VLM Teachers
items.abstract: This paper introduces SAGE, a framework for learning efficient autonomous policies from imperfect Vision-Language Model (VLM) teachers. SAGE selectively queries the VLM only when the learning agent is uncertain, distilling its guidance into a lightweight Reinforcement Learning policy. A key contribution is weighting VLM advice based on environmental feedback, allowing the agent to learn robust policies that outperform unguided RL in complex visual reasoning and navigation tasks.

items.title: Some Emotions Run Deeper: Layer-wise Probing and Causal Intervention in Large Language Models
items.abstract: This paper investigates how Large Language Models (LLMs) represent emotion by analyzing their internal layers across diverse text types. The core method combines layer-wise probing with causal interventions to understand where and how emotion information is processed. The key contribution is demonstrating that the depth at which emotion is accessible in LLMs varies significantly depending on the dataset, suggesting a dynamic interaction between model architecture and textual context.
items.figure_caption: Overview of our experimental pipeline. We localize emotion-sensitive layer bands with layer-wise probing, then evaluate them through online intervention, offline feature scaling, transfer analyses, and early-exit classification.

items.title: When Guardrails Look Effective: Construct Validity Failures in LLM Agent Commerce Evaluation
items.abstract: This paper argues that current evaluations of LLM agents in simulated markets often suffer from construct validity failures, meaning observed economic outcomes don't truly reflect the intended agent behaviors. The authors demonstrate this by showing how seemingly positive welfare gains from marketplace guardrails disappear or even reverse when experimental design choices (like offer schemas) are standardized, highlighting the need for more rigorous evaluation methods.

items.title: Diffusion as a Training Curriculum for Timestep-Free Iterative Reasoning
items.abstract: This paper introduces a novel training curriculum for iterative reasoning models by adapting diffusion models. They achieve this by adding a persistent hidden state to a diffusion denoiser and removing timestep conditioning, allowing for arbitrary inference depth. This "anytime solver" demonstrates impressive accuracy on complex tasks like Sudoku and Maze, even when inference deviates from standard progressive denoising by injecting fresh noise at each step, eliminating the need for parallel processing or external verifiers.
items.figure_caption: Denoiser schematic used for Sudoku-Extreme. The transformer’s attention mask for the example blue target cell is also depicted. We detail architectural modifications for Maze-Unique/Maze-Hard in App. B .

items.title: mzCache: On-Device LLM Memory Management under Multitasking
items.abstract: mzCache addresses the challenge of on-device LLM performance degradation in multitasking mobile environments. Its core method is a novel memory management system that elastically evicts LLM memory and utilizes unified SoC memory for zero-wait GPU inference. The contribution lies in enabling concurrent CPU-side restoration of evicted LLM memory through fine-grained shared buffers, significantly improving responsiveness under unpredictable memory pressure.
items.figure_caption: Figure 1. Multitasking on mobile devices: the user interacts with an on-device LLM service, switches to other apps, and later returns. Memory pressure from concurrent apps evicts LLM memory, increasing the response time from 0.8s to 16s.

items.title: The Structure of Quantization Damage in LLMs: Why the Next Bit Should Be Spent Globally
items.abstract: This paper investigates how quantization, a technique to reduce LLM size, impacts accuracy. It finds that quantization damage is generally spread across many layers, rather than being concentrated in specific "task circuits" or weight statistics. The core contribution is demonstrating that globally distributing a small precision budget to finer quantization granularity is more effective than locally targeting the most "recoverable" layers for improving LLM accuracy.

The band below is the same flight from above, with the \( \delta \) ring on the target and the declaration marked, so the strip and the criterion can be read against each other.

papers.title: GlossoGen: Emergent Language in Complex Multi-Agent LLM Interactions
papers.abstract: GlossoGen is a novel platform designed to study language evolution in complex multi-agent LLM interactions. The paper demonstrates that LLM agents, under pressure and with partial information, can develop compositional and morphologically productive languages that are incomprehensible to humans. Key factors enabling this evolution include efficiency pressure, model strength, and a postmortem stage for convention agreement.
papers.figure_caption: Example of language emergence under budget pressure in an emergency response scenario (example from Sonnet 4.6). In our fictional SaveVeyru scenario, a Field Observer has access to an ailing alien, Veyru. The field observer reports observed symptoms to the Specialist, who can provide remedies which the Observer implements. Agents must handle information asymmetry, forcing them to communicate, and time pressure, encouraging them to develop novel languages, as seen in Round 13.

papers.title: Harness-of-Harness: Multi-Day Autonomous Software Development with Continual Improvement
papers.abstract: This paper introduces Harness-of-Harness (HoH), a framework for multi-day autonomous software development using LLM coding agents. HoH enables continual improvement by organizing agents into iterative planning-coding-testing loops, balancing repair with capability growth and focusing on verifiable increments. Its core contribution is a structured approach to sustained, human-free software development that promotes reuse and maintains project history.
papers.figure_caption: Across successive iterations by Harness-of-Harness, the resulting First-Person-Shooter game features a coherent storyline, implemented combat, weapon and enemy-interaction systems, player guidance, heads-up display and menu systems, cinematic animation, and polished visual and audio presentation, yielding human-playable experience. The game, development traces, and gameplay videos are available on GitHub.

papers.title: The Rise of Verbal Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: This paper introduces Verbal Reinforcement Learning (VRL), a paradigm where natural language serves as the feedback mechanism for language agents. It unifies existing research by categorizing VRL based on when and what verbal feedback modifies, defining three core pillars: language as a grounding signal for task definition, as deliberative feedback for test-time reasoning, and as a learning signal to update model parameters. The contribution lies in providing the first comprehensive framework for understanding and organizing this emerging field.
papers.figure_caption: Language plays three complementary roles in agent’s development lifecycle: grounding the environment, scaffolding intermediate reasoning, and providing learning signal for further training.

papers.title: When Safety Routing Breaks: Understanding Alignment Fragility under Benign Fine-Tuning
papers.abstract: This paper argues that safety alignment in LLMs is fragile due to a "routing pathway" in output-side MLP modules that is selectively re-sharpened by benign fine-tuning. This Fisher-geometric explanation posits that safety Fisher information is low-rank, and fine-tuning flattens the safety geometry while preserving this output pathway. This leads to asymmetric fragility where safety collapses easily, but general utility is less affected, and internal safety representations remain intact.

papers.title: HarnessDev: Can LLMs Create and Evolve Their Own Agent Harness?
papers.abstract: This paper introduces HarnessDev, a benchmark that evaluates an LLM's ability to create and improve its own agent execution infrastructure (harness). Instead of just assessing task outputs, HarnessDev measures how well the LLM can build and refine the underlying system that enables agent functionality. This contributes by shifting evaluation focus to the agent's meta-development capabilities, crucial for deployed agents.

papers.title: A Composable Evaluation System for Reproducible Omni-Modal Foundation Model Evaluation
papers.abstract: This paper introduces OmniEvaluator, a system that addresses the challenge of evaluating omni-modal foundation models by unifying existing, incompatible evaluation toolkits. Its core method connects diverse inference engines and evaluation libraries through a single interface, enabling reproducible benchmarking across text, image, video, and audio. The key contribution is a composable system that simplifies cross-modal evaluation, ensures reproducibility through artifact recording, and facilitates comparison via a shared dashboard.

papers.title: CordisBench: Can Language Models Reason About Component Lifecycles in Dynamic Agent Harnesses?
papers.abstract: This paper introduces CordisBench, a benchmark designed to test language models' ability to reason about component lifecycles in dynamic agent systems where models can modify their own execution environment. The benchmark comprises 1,200 questions covering tasks like identifying affected components and predicting system states after changes, evaluated using a formal runtime called Cordis. The study finds that current models struggle with complex reasoning as the number of relevant interactions increases, particularly in predicting final states and handling reasoning across teardowns.

papers.title: Designing Proactive Thought Partners for Writing
papers.abstract: This paper introduces "proactive thought partners," AI agents designed to offer customizable, higher-level cognitive support during writing, moving beyond basic text suggestions. Through a user study, the research demonstrates that these partners can assist with planning, idea generation, and self-monitoring, with users valuing flexible configuration and non-directive framing. The core contribution lies in designing and evaluating AI that proactively anticipates and supports diverse cognitive needs in the writing process.
papers.figure_caption: Proactive thought partners in the design space of intelligent writing assistants. We position intelligent writing assistants along two dimensions: initiative, distinguishing reactive user-invoked support from proactive system-initiated support, and level of support, distinguishing textual assistance from higher-level cognitive assistance. Proactive thought partners fall within the proactive and cognitive quadrant, where AI offers higher-level cognitive support during writing without requiring explicit user prompting.

papers.title: Efficiently Estimating Optimal Hyperparameter Scaling Laws through Power-Law Entropy Search
papers.abstract: This paper introduces Power-Law Entropy Search (PLES), a novel method for efficiently estimating optimal hyperparameter scaling laws for LLMs. PLES uses a cost-aware Bayesian optimization approach that adaptively experiments to reduce uncertainty in scaling law estimates, rather than optimizing a single objective. Its core contribution is enabling accurate prediction of optimal hyperparameters at large scales with significantly reduced computational cost compared to traditional methods.
papers.figure_caption: Through small-scale experiments that share information across different model and data scales, PLES produces an optimal hyperparameter scaling law estimate ( red line ) that converges to the ground-truth optimal hyperparameter scaling law (black dotted line). In addition, PLES produces uncertainty intervals (red horizontal bars) that indicate our confidence of the scaling law estimate.

papers.title: LEAP: Likelihood Elicitation and Aggregation for LLM-based Probabilistic Forecasting
papers.abstract: This paper introduces LEAP, a novel method for LLM-based probabilistic forecasting that addresses the limitations of monolithic prediction. LEAP elicits likelihood parameters from individual evidence items separately and then aggregates them using an explicit prior and a deterministic probabilistic model. This approach ensures reproducible evidence contributions and allows for flexible forecast types while preserving uncertainty.
papers.figure_caption: The Monolithic baseline can be confidently wrong without revealing which evidence drove the answer. LEAP exposes evidence-level support and combines it through a probabilistic update, making the prediction auditable.

papers.title: Mechanism Design for Alignment and Control
papers.abstract: This paper proposes a mechanism design framework for AI agents with unknown preferences and capabilities. The core method involves a one-sided imitation structure that incentivizes both honest reporting of preferences and obedience to instructions. The contribution lies in characterizing implementable policies and identifying conditions for disciplining multiple agents, with applications to issues like sandbagging and alignment-interpretability trade-offs.

papers.title: Selective Agent Guidance via Entropy: Learning Autonomous Policies from Imperfect VLM Teachers
papers.abstract: This paper introduces SAGE, a framework for learning efficient autonomous policies from imperfect Vision-Language Model (VLM) teachers. SAGE selectively queries the VLM only when the learning agent is uncertain, distilling its guidance into a lightweight Reinforcement Learning policy. A key contribution is weighting VLM advice based on environmental feedback, allowing the agent to learn robust policies that outperform unguided RL in complex visual reasoning and navigation tasks.

papers.title: Some Emotions Run Deeper: Layer-wise Probing and Causal Intervention in Large Language Models
papers.abstract: This paper investigates how Large Language Models (LLMs) represent emotion by analyzing their internal layers across diverse text types. The core method combines layer-wise probing with causal interventions to understand where and how emotion information is processed. The key contribution is demonstrating that the depth at which emotion is accessible in LLMs varies significantly depending on the dataset, suggesting a dynamic interaction between model architecture and textual context.
papers.figure_caption: Overview of our experimental pipeline. We localize emotion-sensitive layer bands with layer-wise probing, then evaluate them through online intervention, offline feature scaling, transfer analyses, and early-exit classification.

papers.title: When Guardrails Look Effective: Construct Validity Failures in LLM Agent Commerce Evaluation
papers.abstract: This paper argues that current evaluations of LLM agents in simulated markets often suffer from construct validity failures, meaning observed economic outcomes don't truly reflect the intended agent behaviors. The authors demonstrate this by showing how seemingly positive welfare gains from marketplace guardrails disappear or even reverse when experimental design choices (like offer schemas) are standardized, highlighting the need for more rigorous evaluation methods.

papers.title: Diffusion as a Training Curriculum for Timestep-Free Iterative Reasoning
papers.abstract: This paper introduces a novel training curriculum for iterative reasoning models by adapting diffusion models. They achieve this by adding a persistent hidden state to a diffusion denoiser and removing timestep conditioning, allowing for arbitrary inference depth. This "anytime solver" demonstrates impressive accuracy on complex tasks like Sudoku and Maze, even when inference deviates from standard progressive denoising by injecting fresh noise at each step, eliminating the need for parallel processing or external verifiers.
papers.figure_caption: Denoiser schematic used for Sudoku-Extreme. The transformer’s attention mask for the example blue target cell is also depicted. We detail architectural modifications for Maze-Unique/Maze-Hard in App. B .

papers.title: mzCache: On-Device LLM Memory Management under Multitasking
papers.abstract: mzCache addresses the challenge of on-device LLM performance degradation in multitasking mobile environments. Its core method is a novel memory management system that elastically evicts LLM memory and utilizes unified SoC memory for zero-wait GPU inference. The contribution lies in enabling concurrent CPU-side restoration of evicted LLM memory through fine-grained shared buffers, significantly improving responsiveness under unpredictable memory pressure.
papers.figure_caption: Figure 1. Multitasking on mobile devices: the user interacts with an on-device LLM service, switches to other apps, and later returns. Memory pressure from concurrent apps evicts LLM memory, increasing the response time from 0.8s to 16s.

papers.title: The Structure of Quantization Damage in LLMs: Why the Next Bit Should Be Spent Globally
papers.abstract: This paper investigates how quantization, a technique to reduce LLM size, impacts accuracy. It finds that quantization damage is generally spread across many layers, rather than being concentrated in specific "task circuits" or weight statistics. The core contribution is demonstrating that globally distributing a small precision budget to finer quantization granularity is more effective than locally targeting the most "recoverable" layers for improving LLM accuracy.
